lines.text: A pimple begins deep inside a pore, long before you see anything.
Usually, old cells drift up and out with the oil.
But sometimes they cling together instead.
Oil and cells pack into a tiny plug… and the doorway starts to close.
If the top stays open, the plug can darken in the air. That's a blackhead, and that dark color isn't dirt.
If skin closes over it, it stays pale.
Behind the plug, oil keeps arriving. With nowhere to go, the pore slowly swells.
The microbes inside have a feast… and your body notices.
Immune cells gather, and the spot turns red, warm, and swollen.
That's the pimple you finally see. A small, blocked doorway… and your body, working to clear it.
